tickerText: [TENNIS] Wimbledon 2026 Day 5 Friday, July 3: the third round opens at the All England Club after Day 4 saw defending champion Iga Świątek cruise past Karolina Plíšková 6-1, 6-3 and Elena Rybakina dismantle Caty McNally 6-1, 6-2 — Centre Court Friday features Aryna Sabalenka vs Jelena Ostapenko and Coco Gauff vs Claire Liu while Novak Djokovic faces Arthur Rinderknech and Jannik Sinner meets Jenson Brooksby in the men's last 32 • [SQUASH] HCL-SRFI PSA Challenger finals day Friday at Juhu Vile Parle Gymkhana in Mumbai — Egypt's Yassin Shohdy and Malaysia's Mohammad Syafiq Kamal contest the men's title after Shohdy ended top seed Velavan Senthilkumar's run 11-4, 11-8, 11-5, while India's Tanvi Khanna faces second seed Farida Walid in the women's final after a five-game semifinal win over Akari Midorikawa • [BADMINTON] YONEX Canada Open 2026 quarterfinals Friday at Markham Pan Am Centre — Lee Zii Jia targets his first World Tour semifinal in two years against Chinese Taipei's Wang Po-Wei after sweeping Liao Jhuo-Fu 21-11, 21-13, with home top seeds Victor Lai and Michelle Li chasing deep runs at the $250K BWF Super 300 through Sunday, July 5 • [PICKLEBALL] Sansan PPA Asia 500 Tokyo Open semifinal day at Arena Tachikawa Tachihi — Rika Fujiwara and Seiya Hatakeyama lead Japan's charge in singles while Fujiwara and 15-year-old Kyo Sawaki battle for women's doubles gold after a 2-1 quarterfinal thriller, with medal matches set for Saturday across the $50,000 capital debut • [TABLE TENNIS] WTT United States Smash 2026 singles Round of 16 and mixed doubles semifinals Friday at the Ontario Convention Center — Sun Yingsha advanced 11-9, 11-3, 11-6 over Nina Mittelham and Wang Chuqin faces Anders Lind after a 3-2 mixed doubles comeback with Sun over Alexis Lebrun and Satsuki Odo, as Kanak Jha and India's doubles pairs exit in quarterfinals at the $1.55M Grand Smash through July 5

newsItems.title: Świątek and Rybakina Storm Into Wimbledon Third Round
newsItems.excerpt: Wimbledon 2026 reached the end of the second round on Thursday, July 2, and the defending women's champion delivered a statement on Centre Court. Iga Świątek needed just 69 minutes to overpower Karolina Plíšková 6-1, 6-3, winning 26 of 35 points in the opening set and extending her streak of never losing before the third round at a Grand Slam since the 2019 US Open. Two-time major winner Elena Rybakina was equally ruthless, dismantling American Caty McNally 6-1, 6-2 with four breaks and a flawless service hold record. Amanda Anisimova survived a 10-point third-set tiebreak to beat Sofia Kenin 6-2, 4-6, 7-6 (3), while Alexander Zverev and Taylor Fritz joined the third-round field with straight-set wins. Friday, July 3, opens the last 32 with Sabalenka-Ostapenko and Gauff-Liu on the women's side and Djokovic-Rinderknech and Sinner-Brooksby in the men's draw.

newsItems.title: Tanvi Khanna Reaches Mumbai Final as Senthilkumar Exits
newsItems.excerpt: The HCL-SRFI PSA Challenger Squash Tournament in Mumbai reaches championship day Friday, July 3, at the Juhu Vile Parle Gymkhana Club. India's Tanvi Khanna kept home hopes alive by outlasting Japan's Akari Midorikawa 11-4, 9-11, 11-7, 3-11, 11-4 in a 44-minute semifinal to set up a women's final against Egypt's second seed Farida Walid, who beat Nour Khafagy 11-8, 10-12, 11-4, 11-9. The men's draw will be decided without an Indian champion after top seed Velavan Senthilkumar fell to Yassin Shohdy 11-4, 11-8, 11-5, while Mohammad Syafiq Kamal survived a rollercoaster five-game win over Ziad Ibrahim 2-11, 11-1, 8-11, 11-6, 11-9. Shohdy and Kamal meet for the $15,000 men's title as Khanna bids to deny Walid in the women's final at the $30,000 combined event.

newsItems.title: Lee Zii Jia Eyes Canada Open Semifinal Breakthrough
newsItems.excerpt: The YONEX Canada Open 2026 moves into quarterfinals Friday, July 3, at the Markham Pan Am Centre with Malaysia's Lee Zii Jia one win from his first World Tour semifinal in more than two years. Lee dispatched Chinese Taipei's Liao Jhuo-Fu 21-11, 21-13 in just 29 minutes on Thursday, backing up a first-round walkover when India's Kidambi Srikanth retired trailing 11-10. He now faces Wang Po-Wei, who reached the last eight with a dominant 21-5, 21-13 win over Denmark's Ditlev Jaeger Holm. The $250,000 BWF Super 300 event also has Canada's top seeds Victor Lai and Michelle Li chasing deep runs on home soil, with semifinals Saturday and finals Sunday, July 5. A quarterfinal victory would mark another step in Lee's ranking rebuild after an injury-hit spell that dropped him outside the world's top 100 earlier this year.

newsItems.title: Fujiwara and Hatakeyama Lead Japan Into Tokyo Open Semifinals
newsItems.excerpt: The PPA Asia 500 Sansan Tokyo Open reaches semifinal day Friday, July 3, at Arena Tachikawa Tachihi in the Japanese capital's first PPA Tour Asia stop. Rika Fujiwara, who captured Japan's first PPA Asia singles gold at Macau in May, advanced in women's singles alongside men's semifinalist Seiya Hatakeyama after Day 2 main-draw action. Fujiwara also reached the women's doubles last four with 15-year-old partner Kyo Sawaki, rallying past China's Yufei Long and Australia's Andy Dicosabrevich 2-1 (12-10, 9-11, 12-10) in a tense quarterfinal. Hatakeyama beat fellow Japanese pro Kenta Miyoshi in the Round of 16 before dispatching Malaysia's Jimmy Lyong Kai Long 11-7, 11-5, while Yuta Funakoshi and 15-year-old Tama Shimabukuro reached the men's doubles semifinals. Medal matches across all five pro disciplines are set for Saturday, July 4, at the $50,000 event that drew more than 800 registered players.
